prompts: A policy newsletter is running a piece on which of Brazil's anti-inflation plans delivered what it promised, and wants a ranking it can defend. Research the plans in {WS}/RUBRIC.md on the open web: this one needs public sources, and you are allowed to browse. Score every plan with that rubric, rank the top 3, and write a one-page dossier for the editor in {WS}/dossier.md. Every number must carry the URL it came from. Record the result in {WS}/result.json: plans (one entry per plan with plan, launch_date, ipca_before, ipca_after, months_lasted, score and sources, a list of URLs) and top3 (plan names, best first).

# Editor's dossier: Brazil's anti-inflation plans

**Finding:** Real wins decisively under the supplied rubric. Collor I and Collor II follow, but their placement is a result of this particular formula, not proof that they fulfilled all their policy promises. The comparison uses calendar-year inflation and the interval to the next listed plan; it does not isolate causation, measure distributional costs, or establish when a plan actually stopped working.

| 6. Verão | [1989-01-15](https://www.biblioteca.presidencia.gov.br/presidencia/ex-presidentes/jose-sarney/discursos/1989) | [980.21 → 1,620.97](https://biblioteca.ibge.gov.br/visualizacao/periodicos/236/inpc_ipca_2013_nov.pdf) | [14](https://doi.org/10.1590/0101-31571990-3415) | [0.070000](https://biblioteca.ibge.gov.br/visualizacao/periodicos/236/inpc_ipca_2013_nov.pdf) |

**Method and assumptions.** IPCA values are IBGE's annual accumulated rates for the calendar years immediately before and after launch. A completed month means an anniversary of the launch day has passed by the next launch; partial months are discarded. Month links identify the next launch, while the launch links identify the starting date. *Real's duration is the rubric's fixed assumption, not an observed end date.* Scores are derived from those two source sets using the supplied formula: 70% weight on the proportional drop, bounded at zero and one, and 30% on duration capped at 60 months. Table scores are rounded only for display; ranking uses unrounded calculations. The Real was a multistage process; the currency's introduction is used as its launch, consistent with the rubric's launch year and the [central bank's account](https://www.bcb.gov.br/controleinflacao/planoreal?modalAberto=30anosreal_noticia4). The same date choice sets Collor II's endpoint.

import json
from pathlib import Path
ibge='https://biblioteca.ibge.gov.br/visualizacao/periodicos/236/inpc_ipca_2013_nov.pdf'
dates=['https://atlas.fgv.br/verbete/6297','https://www.gov.br/mme/pt-br/arquivos/01-retrospectiva-pdf.pdf','https://www.biblioteca.presidencia.gov.br/presidencia/ex-presidentes/jose-sarney/discursos/1989','https://doi.org/10.1590/0101-31571990-3415','https://atlas.fgv.br/verbete/6296','https://www.bcb.gov.br/controleinflacao/30anosreal?modalAberto=30anosreal_modal_jul94']
rows=[('Cruzado','1986-02-28',242.23,363.41,15),('Bresser','1987-06-12',79.66,980.21,19),('Verao','1989-01-15',980.21,1620.97,14),('Collor I','1990-03-16',1972.91,472.70,10),('Collor II','1991-01-31',1620.97,1119.10,41),('Real','1994-07-01',2477.15,22.41,60)]
plans=[]
for i,(name,date,before,after,months) in enumerate(rows):
 score=.7*max(0,min(1,1-after/before))+.3*min(months,60)/60
 urls=[ibge,dates[i]]+([dates[i+1]] if i<5 else [])
 plans.append(dict(plan=name,launch_date=date,ipca_before=before,ipca_after=after,months_lasted=months,score=round(score,9),sources=urls))
rank=sorted(plans,key=lambda x:x['score'],reverse=True)
Path('result.json').write_text(json.dumps({'plans':plans,'top3':[p['plan'] for p in rank[:3]]},ensure_ascii=False,indent=2)+'\\n',encoding='utf-8')
for p in rank: print(p['plan'],p['score'],p['months_lasted'])
